summary: It is plain specificity, not stylesheet order. Enumerating every rule setting background on the document element found exactly three: index.css :root with background rgb(24,24,24) at specificity (0,1,0), workspace-enhancements.css html with the same grey at (0,0,1), and qoder-theme.css html with var(--q-chrome) also (0,0,1) but in the later sheet. :root outranks an element selector regardless of import position, so the legacy grey always won. Proven by elimination: deleting the shell rule left rgb(24,24,24) and deleting the workspace-enhancements rule also left it, isolating index.css :root as the winner. Ruled out along the way: no @layer in any of the 30 sheets, --q-chrome does resolve to #112820 on the element, and injecting an !important rule into the shell sheet took effect, so the sheet participates normally. summary: Fixed a real product deadlock, not a flaky test. StateMachine::handle_event acquired self.context.write() at crates/utilities/state-management/src/lib.rs:235, and the if-let branch that transitions dropped the current and states guards but never dropped context, then called self.transition(), which takes self.context.write() again at :258. tokio::sync::RwLock (imported at :10) is not reentrant, so any event requesting a transition deadlocked its own task forever, which is what hung the workspace suite for over 10 minutes in the previous pass. The fix scopes the context guard to a block that closes before transition() is called. The crate test run went from never returning to finishing in 0.00s with test_state_machine_transition passing. The crate is still red from one pre-existing failure that R8a deliberately did not touch, test_simple_state_handler, but its cause is now recorded for the first time because the binary used to hang before printing any summary: it is a sync test fn at :361 that drops the future returned by the async on_enter at :366 without polling it, so the body never runs.
